Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

trick verb

deceive

also deceive, fool, take in, play a trick on, be tricked, fall for, feed someone a line, he’s feeding you a line, string someone along, be taken in, they know they were taken in, play games with, stop playing games, make a fool of, pull a fast one on, con, pull the wool over someone’s eyes, play tricks on

classical

Plaut. Rud. 4.7.9: ubi dēcipiuntur dolīs (Lewis & Short)
Phaedr. 1.13.12: corvī dēceptus stupor

dēcipiō, dēcipere, dēcēpī, dēceptum

verb, third conjugation

trick, deceive, catch out

Literally to catch, as in a snare (dēcipula, a trap).

Other words

  • fallō, fallere, fefellī, falsum — deceive, trick

    verb, third conjugation · also used · classical · Ter. Eun. 385; Traupman 312: fall for a trick, fallī

    The wider word: besides deceiving it means to escape someone’s notice and to let them down (nisi mē fallit animus, Cic.; spēs fefellit).

  • verba dare — fool, hoodwink (with the dative)

    phrase · also used · classical · Ter. And. 211; Cic. Att. 15.16a (Lewis & Short); Traupman 102: verba tibi iste dat; Traupman 106: pull a fast one on, verba dare (+ dat.); Traupman 295

    (vōx sermōnis cotīdiānī: Ter.; Cic. in epistulīs)

    “Give someone (mere) words”: to fool them, never to give one’s word (see word).

  • lūdōs facere (aliquem) — make a fool of, make game of

    phrase: the person made sport of in the accusative, sometimes the dative · also used · classical · Plaut. Capt. 3.4.47: ut nunc is tē lūdōs facit (Lewis & Short s.v. lūdus); Plaut. Aul. 2.2.74 (Lewis & Short); Traupman 105: stop playing games, dēsiste lūdōs facere; Traupman 398

    (vōx cōmica: Plaut., Ter.)

  • lūdificō, lūdificāre, lūdificāvī, lūdificātum — make a fool of

    verb, first conjugation · also used · classical · Traupman 317

    (vōx cōmica: Plaut., Ter.)

  • lūdificor, lūdificārī, lūdificātus sum — make a fool of, play a trick on

    also used · classical · Plaut. Mil. 4.4.25 (Lewis & Short); Traupman 361

  • ōs sublinere alicui — cheat, make a fool of (literally: smear someone’s face)

    also used · classical · Plaut. (Lewis & Short s.v. ōs and sublinō); Traupman 366

    (vōx cōmica: Plaut.)

Examples

  • tunc dēmum ingemuit corvī dēceptus stupor

    only then did the foolish crow, tricked, groanPhaedr. 1.13.12

  • nunc referam grātiam atque eās itidem fallam, ut ab īs fallimur?

    shall I now pay them back and trick them just as we’re tricked by them?Ter. Eun. 385

  • quoi verba dare difficilest

    a man who is hard to foolTer. And. 211

  • Sciunt sibi data esse verba.

    They know that they were taken in.Traupman 109

  • Dēsiste lūdōs facere.

    Stop playing games.Traupman 105

  • alicui verba dare

    to take someone in (to con someone)Traupman 389

  • subdolum (-am) esse adversus aliquem

    to pull the wool over someone’s eyesTraupman 366

See also trick, lie, word.
